results.name: a person without room.design cannot create a room (403)
the designer creates the room: 201 with a canonical room code
the room is PLANNED with declared dimensions and no devices yet
all ten devices are added, each with a tenant-unique canonical asset id
before the camera is added, Lite’s required-equipment rule opens a High design deficiency: the room type needs a camera
with the camera in the design the deficiency is resolved, and the camera is proposed into the video path (camera → room compute) and the network
no open High/Critical design deficiency remains; the plan is compiled server-side with applicable tests
the designer saves revision 2 with its SHA-256
a revision with nothing changed is refused (422)
the designer cannot approve the classification (403)
the systems engineer approves the suggested classification
the designer generates the drawing set (seven drawings, GENERATED)
the designer cannot approve a drawing (403)
the systems engineer approves all seven drawings
the designer cannot approve the design (403: room.design.approve)
one governed step at a time: PLANNED → COMMISSIONING is refused (422)
the systems engineer approves the design (DESIGN_APPROVED)
the installer cannot open the installation window (403: window.approve)
the operations lead approves the installation window (INSTALLATION_PENDING)
the installer records the installation (INSTALLED_UNVERIFIED)
the installer cannot start commissioning (403: plan.compile)
the systems engineer starts commissioning (COMMISSIONING)
the room is COMMISSIONING, the approved revision is 2, every applicable test is NOT_TESTED and needs physical execution
the systems engineer holds no evidence-upload authority (403); the commissioning engineer files the engineering records for the tests the systems engineer records
one evidence object per applicable test is stored with its SHA-256 and a retention date (75)
an evidence file reads back byte-for-byte (its hash re-verified on read)
the designer is not a responsible role for a commissioning test (403)
an evidence kind the test does not accept is refused (422)
every applicable test is recorded by its responsible role and is PASS_UNVERIFIED (syseng 17, service 34, cxeng 16, dsp_eng 5, video_eng 2, control_eng 1)
self-verification is refused: the commissioning engineer cannot verify a result they recorded (422)
the field technician holds no verification authority (403)
every result is PASS_VERIFIED by a different person (cxeng 59, qa_reviewer 16)
a result is never verified twice (422)
the systems engineer cannot accept the room (403: customer.accept)
the QA reviewer verified results of this room and is refused the acceptance (422, separation of duties)
the QA reviewer lends customer.accept to the operations lead, scoped and expiring (ADR-0005)
the operations lead — neither recorder nor verifier — accepts the room through the delegation (200)
baseline v1 exists and is CURRENT
v1 binds the approved design revision 2, its hash, the plan, every applicable result PASS_VERIFIED and every evidence object
substituting the camera of the ACCEPTED room directly is refused (422) and the refusal names recommissioning
the installer cannot recommission the room (403: plan.compile)
the systems engineer recommissions the room (ACCEPTED → COMMISSIONING)
baseline v1 stays CURRENT while the room is recommissioned
the installer cannot change the design (403: room.design)
during recommissioning a device is not moved: only a model substitution is accepted (422)
the designer substitutes the camera model (200); the response names the tests the substitution reopens
the camera keeps its asset id, carries the new model, and its model history keeps the previous model
no other device changed: same ten asset ids
the designer saves revision 3
the comparison of the accepted revision 2 with revision 3 shows exactly the camera swap
baseline v1 is byte-for-byte unchanged (same JSON before and after the change) and still CURRENT
Assurance assesses the room against baseline v1 and reports the substitution on the register as drift (recorded, not measured)
the remedy proposed is a fix that needs an engineer’s approval, and live health stays NOT_MONITORED
readiness reports the recommissioning against baseline v1 and the substitution (asset, from, to)
it names the tests that must be re-run on the new camera, each with its reasons and its responsible role
every test whose plan row names the camera is required again, and the asset-identity check is required after the substitution
tests that do not depend on the camera are not reopened
re-acceptance is blocked with the reasons: the design change needs an approved revision, the reopened tests must be re-run, and the approved drawings no longer match
the drawing check opens design deficiencies for the approved equipment schedule and placement plan that no longer match
the outstanding actions name who must do what: approve revision 3 (not its author) and re-run per responsible role
completion counts only the results that still count: the reopened tests are not verified any more
an attempt to re-accept now is refused (422) with the same reasons
the designer (the author of revision 3) holds no design approval (403)
the systems engineer approves revision 3: the re-acceptance will bind it
a revision is approved once (422)
the regenerated drawings are approved again and the drawing deficiencies resolve
the design requirement is met; the only blocker left is re-running the reopened tests on the new camera
baseline v1 is still byte-for-byte unchanged and CURRENT after the design approval
the relationship graph places the camera in its room and feeding the room compute, and connects it to the switch
downstream impact of the camera includes the devices it feeds (the room compute and onwards)
Search Party returns the camera’s neighbourhood with edge provenance
Search Party answers “what depends on this camera?” with the downstream devices and the affected room
Search Party lists the camera’s connections (signal to the compute, network to the switch), marked as design-proposed
the room reads back COMMISSIONING (recommissioning) with revision 3 approved and every device
the baseline lineage holds v1 (CURRENT) and no other version
the service history reads (no work order was needed: no test failed) with the room’s issue events
the designer cannot read the audit trail (403)
the Evidence Ledger chain verifies end to end (data steward)
the room’s 364 audit events are sealed into the chain, in order (sequence, id and time agree)

the Room Story reads in order: created → design approved → window → installed → commissioning → results → verification → baseline v1 published by the acceptance → recommissioned → camera replaced → revision approved
the refusals of the scenario are in the trail too (DENIED, with the actor’s role)
the acceptance is audited as delegated, naming the delegation and its grantor
the domain events of the change were delivered by the outbox: room.device_swapped, commission.asset_replaced, room.design_approved
the operational read model is rebuilt from the events: COMMISSIONING, live health NOT_MONITORED
the 27 KPI passports compute over the records, each with arithmetic or a stated reason (never a silent 0)
the building rollup computes the Northstar Annex from its own rooms, and the units add up to the estate
Mission Control reads for the systems engineer
the KPI summary counts the scenario’s verified results and reports operational performance NOT_MONITORED
